question: Does Baleta and Baleta (2016) provide reliable Palanan species-by-site or seasonal occurrence evidence, or a historical landing-name lead only?

source.citation: Baleta, A. N., Jr., & Baleta, F. N. (2016). Species composition of marine food fishes at Palanan, Isabela as influenced by seasonal variation. International Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Studies, 4(3), 414–420.
source.publisherMetadata: The PDF first-page header gives 2016, 4(3), pages 414–420 and a copyright notice; its running header instead prints 4(2), so issue metadata conflicts within the document.
source.authorsAffiliation: Both authors are listed with the Institute of Fisheries, Isabela State University.
source.copyrightAndReuse: The article displays © 2016 IJFAS. No item-specific open license or permission to redistribute its list, figures, or reported photos was verified.

retrievalFollowUp.publisherDirectPdf: Direct HTTPS retrieval returned HTTP 403; the browser PDF open and page screenshot routes also rejected the publisher URL as restricted.
retrievalFollowUp.indexedText: A search-indexed extraction of the publisher PDF was available, but its table flow contains column/row alignment noise and OCR-like spelling inconsistencies.
retrievalFollowUp.pageImageReview: Not completed: no page image was available from the publisher through the checked retrieval routes.
retrievalFollowUp.disposition: Do not transcribe the 74-name table or treat the indexed text as visually verified. Seek a readable publisher, author, or institutional-library copy, then manually check table rows and bibliography images.

reportedScope.locality: Four fish landing stations in Palanan, Isabela: Dicotcotan, Sabang, Culasi and Dimolid.
reportedScope.methodAsReported: Ocular inspection and interviews with 40 fishers and/or vendors (10 per landing area); the article says the interviews occurred at the onset of summer (April) and rainy season (October), and that photo documentation was gathered.
reportedScope.identificationAsReported: The paper names field guides for Tayabas Bay and Palawan and FishBase for final verification. The accessible article does not identify vouchers or provide a verifiable photo-to-taxon archive.
reportedScope.temporalLimit: The article does not state the calendar year or exact dates for the April and October sampling/interviews. It does not establish annual or current presence.
reportedScope.tableScope: Table 1 presents a pooled list with scientific, English, Filipino and Paranan names. Table 2 presents a pooled summer-versus-rainy-season list; the article does not provide a verified species-by-landing-site matrix or capture coordinates.

conflictsAndLimits: The paper prints 7°3′32″ N, 122°25′47″ E as the study-area coordinate. This is held as suspect for the stated Palanan/Isabela locality and is not used to georeference any record; the article gives no corrected station coordinates.
The abstract names Acanthurus lineatus, whereas Table 1 spells it Acanthurus lineathus. Other table and family spellings also need image-level and taxonomic verification before normalization.
The paper says 74 species; its results report 52 genera, 37 families and 9 orders. These are source claims, not an independently checked count or an app checklist.
Landing-site records describe fish reported or seen at market/landing contexts, not confirmed capture coordinates or occurrence inside the adjacent municipal-water polygon.

The paper does not specify the sampling year, survey effort beyond the interviews, fisher sampling frame, catch-landing inclusion rules, vouchers, station coordinates, or reproducible species-by-site counts.
The article's season labels and discussion use broader seasonal periods without supplying exact sample dates; do not turn the pooled April/October comparison into a monthly calendar or season rule.

No source-specific license was verified. Public access to the PDF is not treated as permission for public-app reproduction. The paper's claimed photo documentation was not used as a Bangwit image source.

disposition.sourceUse: Research-only historical Palanan landing and vernacular-name lead; consider for a later manually checked taxonomic crosswalk, not for present-day species occurrence.

nextAction: Obtain a readable publisher, author, or institutional-library copy because the publisher PDF returned HTTP 403 and available indexed text does not preserve table alignment. Then inspect table/bibliography page images, reconcile each printed spelling and count against authoritative fish taxonomy, identify any specimen or photo vouchers, recover exact sampling year and station/capture crosswalk, and confirm item-specific reuse permission. Until then, keep all 74 reported names untranscribed and research-only. Keep this source separate from the 2017 Isabela-wide landings paper and do not sum their aggregate species counts.

sources.supports: Publisher-indexed article text for landing stations, interview/ocular method, April/October season labels, aggregate taxon claims, field guide/FishBase identification method, printed coordinate and internal volume/species-name discrepancies. Direct PDF retrieval returned HTTP 403 during the 2026-11-20 follow-up, so page-image verification of table layout and bibliography remains pending.
